Acting Chief Executive | chief2_name = | chief2_position = | parent_agency = | child1_agency = | website = [http://www.cera.govt.nz cera.govt.nz] | footnotes = }} The '''Canterbury Earthquake Recovery Authority''' ('''CERA'''; [[Māori language|Māori]]: ''Te Mana Haumanu ki Waitaha'') was the public service department of New Zealand charged with coordinating the rebuild of [[Christchurch]] and the surrounding areas following the [[2011 Christchurch earthquake|22 February 2011 earthquake]]. After it was disestablished on 18 April 2016, CERA's functions were taken over by a variety of other agencies. ==Description== CERA was formed in response to the February 2011 Christchurch earthquake, and its establishment was announced late March 2011. It had wide-ranging powers and could suspend laws and regulations for the purpose of earthquake recovery.{{cite press release |url= http://www.beehive.govt.nz/release/new-authority-will-deliver-canterbury |title= New authority will deliver for Canterbury |publisher=New Zealand Government |date=29 March 2011 |access-date=31 March 2011}} The department operated for five years, with annual reviews.{{cite news |url= http://www.stuff.co.nz/business/4819195/Five-year-task-for-Christchurch-earthquake-recovery-agency |title=Five-year quake rebuild task |author=Martin Kay and John Hartevelt |work=Stuff|publisher=Fairfax |date=29 March 2011 |access-date=31 March 2011}} CERA was disestablished on 18 April 2016.{{cite web |title=CERA has been disestablished| url=http://cera.govt.nz/| access-date=9 June 2016| publisher=Department for the Prime Minister and Cabinet}} [[Roger Sutton]] commenced as CERA's CEO on 13 June 2011.{{cite news |title=Roger Sutton appointed quake recovery czar |url=http://www.stuff.co.nz/national/christchurch-earthquake/4995119/Roger-Sutton-appointed-quake-recovery-czar|access-date=12 May 2011 |work=Stuff |date=12 May 2011}} He had previously been CEO of [[Orion New Zealand Limited|Orion New Zealand]], the electricity distribution company for the Christchurch area. Sutton resigned as CEO on 17 November 2014 effective on 31 January 2015 when CERA was downgraded from a public service department to a departmental agency within the [[Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet (New Zealand)|Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet]] (DPMC).{{cite web|url=http://beehive.govt.nz/release/statement-resignation-roger-sutton|title=beehive.govt.nz – Statement on the resignation of Roger Sutton|work=beehive.govt.nz|access-date=20 September 2015}} [[John Ombler]], CERA's establishment CEO was appointed on 19 November 2014 effective on 1 December to be Acting CEO until a permanent Chief Executive is named.{{cite web|url=http://beehive.govt.nz/release/minister-welcomes-appointment-john-ombler|title=beehive.govt.nz – Minister welcomes appointment of John Ombler|work=beehive.govt.nz|access-date=20 September 2015}}{{cite web|url=http://www.nbr.co.nz/article/acting-cera-boss-appointed-sutton-sent-home-ng-165588|title=Acting CERA boss appointed, Sutton sent home|work=The National Business Review|access-date=20 September 2015}} CERA received criticism for paying panel members $1000 per day,{{cite news |title='Outrage' over $1000 a day pay for panel |first=David |last=Williams |url= http://www.stuff.co.nz/the-press/news/christchurch-earthquake-2011/5311304/Outrage-over-1000-a-day-pay-for-panel |work=[[The Press]] |date=20 August 2011 |access-date=11 November 2012}} approximately 10 times the national average.{{cite web| url=http://www.stats.govt.nz/browse_for_stats/income-and-work/Income/NZIncomeSurvey_HOTPJun11qtr.aspx| title=New Zealand Income Survey: June 2011 quarter| publisher=Statistics New Zealand| date=6 October 2011}} CERA's powers were challenged in the [[High Court of New Zealand|High Court]] after it ordered the demolition of [[Wharetiki House]] at 854 [[Colombo Street]]. The owner of the house wanted to restore it after it had suffered damage in the February 2011 earthquake. Justice Whata dismissed the challenge on 20 June 2011, and the building was demolished the following day.{{cite news |last=Heather |first=Ben |title=Bid to save historic house fails |url=http://www.stuff.co.nz/the-press/news/christchurch-earthquake-2011/5343977/Bid-to-save-historic-house-fails |access-date=27 July 2011 |work=[[The Press]] |date=27 July 2011 |page=A12}} In October 2011, CERA hoped to have all of the [[Christchurch Central City]] open again in April 2012.{{cite news|last=Heather |first=Ben |title=City Mall opening may be delayed |url= http://www.stuff.co.nz/the-press/news/christchurch-earthquake-2011/5788835/City-Mall-opening-may-be-delayed |access-date=23 October 2011|work=[[The Press]] |date=15 October 2011}} In April 2012 the Christchurch Central Development Unit (CCDU) was established as a unit within CERA to focus on rebuilding the central business district of Christchurch, led by [[Warwick Isaacs]].{{cite press release |title=New unit for the rebuild of central Christchurch |url= http://www.beehive.govt.nz/release/new-unit-rebuild-central-christchurch |publisher=New Zealand Government |date=18 April 2012 |access-date=11 November 2012}} A public consultation on the organisation's transport plan closed on 1 February 2013.{{cite news| url= http://www.3news.co.nz/Christchurch-residents-urged-to-contribute-to-CCDU-plan/tabid/423/articleID/284253/Default.aspx| work= 3 News NZ| title= Chch residents urged to contribute to plan| date= 24 January 2013| access-date= 23 January 2013| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20130412224343/http://www.3news.co.nz/Christchurch-residents-urged-to-contribute-to-CCDU-plan/tabid/423/articleID/284253/Default.aspx| archive-date= 12 April 2013| url-status= dead}} As of October 2013, Cabinet had not signed off on the plan. At its peak, the organisation employed 357 staff. Its functions were taken over by [[Land Information New Zealand]] (LINZ), the [[Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment]] (MBIE), and the [[Ministry of Health (New Zealand)|Ministry of Health]] in December 2015, and the DPMC on 1 March 2016. Within the DPMC, the Greater Christchurch Group is responsible for part of the functions that CERA used to carry out. In April 2016, other functions went to newly established and existing organisations: the Crown company Otakaro Ltd (responsible for delivering anchor projects) and the council-Crown agency [[Regenerate Christchurch]] (responsible for developing regeneration plans for Christchurch, including the [[residential red zone]]) and Christchurch City Council (coordinating the Canterbury Public Sector Work Health & Safety Working Group). When CERA was disbanded, it still had 170 staff.{{cite news| last1=Wright| first1=Michael| last2=Hume| first2=Myles| title=More than 100 Cera staff get new rebuild jobs| url=http://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/78989835/more-than-100-cera-staff-get-new-rebuild-jobs.html| access-date=9 June 2016| work=[[The Press]]| date=17 April 2016}} A report released by the [[Controller and Auditor-General of New Zealand|auditor-general]] in February 2017 was critical of CERA's performance, citing tensions with [[Christchurch City Council]] as one of the reasons for delays with implementing projects. CERA was praised for the effective production of the [[Christchurch Central Recovery Plan]], but then was "less successful" with the implementation of the various projects that the plan had identified. The minister who had been responsible for CERA, [[Gerry Brownlee]], dismissed the report as "unbalanced", while the mayor of Christchurch, [[Lianne Dalziel]], stated that she "always believed the recovery should be a collaborative partnership between the Crown and council".{{cite news |last1=Truebridge |first1=Nick |last2=Redmond |first2=Adele |title=Tensions 'delayed rebuild'|url= http://www.stuff.co.nz/the-press/business/the-rebuild/89207000/tensions-between-cera-and-christchurch-city-council-delayed-rebuild-report-says |access-date=9 February 2017 |work=[[The Press]] |date=9 February 2017 |page=A1}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== {{Commons category}} *[http://www.cera.govt.nz Expired CERA homepage] {{NZ Public Service Departments}} {{Christchurch earthquakes}} {{Authority control}} [[Category:New Zealand public service departmental agencies]] [[Category:Canterbury Region]] [[Category:2011 Christchurch earthquake]] [[Category:2011 establishments in New Zealand]] [[Category:2016 disestablishments in New Zealand]]
